1. This Writ Petition has been filed, to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the 1st Respondent to consider the representation of the Petitioner dated 27.11.2023, in accordance with Section 56(1)(b)
of the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971, within a stipulated time.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. This court heard the learned counsel on either side and considered their submissions and also carefully perused the materials placed on record.
3. In the representation of the Petitioner, the Petitioner has made few allegations, indicating that the 5th Respondent has put up an unauthorised construction.
The contention of the Petitioner is that the 5th Respondent, after getting approval for 24 apartments, has constructed 30 apartments.
The serious allegation that the Petitioner has made in his representation is that the 5th Respondent did not execute UDS for the entire extent of land.
It appears that there is a dispute between the Petitioner and the builder with regard to UDS.
The Petitioner appears to believe that the builder has given only lesser extent of UDS.
This cannot be resolved in a Writ Petition.

4. Even the Official Respondents are not competent to decide such https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis representation and or as to whether the Petitioner can enforce his contractual right as to what extent they are entitled to.
The construction put up by the 5th Respondent is given to the Petitioner, who also obtained sale deed from the builder.
The Petitioner's representation is based on their right and privileges according to his interpretation of the construction agreement.
It cannot be resolved by the Official Respondents.

5. The learned counsel for the 5th Respondent has pointed out that the 5th Respondent did not convey the right in respect of substantial portion of the land consciously as the building plan itself was obtained subject to the area being shown as vacant site and made available.
It is now represented that the portion in front of the building had been acquired.
Only in the context of making a claim for the amount to be disbursed by way of compensation for the land acquired, the Petitioner appears to have approached this Court, by way of this Writ Petition.
This Court or the Official Respondents cannot resolve such disputes or any other issue between the Petitioner and the builder, arising out of contract.

Therefore, this Writ Petition is devoid of merits and liable to be K.Jeyasabarinathan vs The Chennai Metropolitan Development ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44451155/
2 dismissed.

6. With the above observation, this Writ Petition is dismissed.
No costs.
